citation: Bottge, B. A., Ma, X., Gassaway, L., Toland, M. D., Butler, M., & Cho, S.-J. (2014). Effects of Blended Instructional Models on Math Performance. Exceptional Children, 80(4), 423-437. https://doi.org/10.1177/0014402914527240
design: Pretest-posttest cluster-randomized RCT; assignment at SCHOOL level. 31 middle schools analyzed (15 EAI + 16 BAU; originally 16/16 but one EAI school dropped before pretest), 49 special-education teachers, 64 resource rooms, 335 students WITH DISABILITIES (MMD, OHI, SLD, autism, EBD) taught in pullout resource rooms. Intervention = Enhanced Anchored Instruction (EAI), a blended curriculum of explicit fraction-computation instruction + video-anchored problem solving + hands-on projects (5 units); comparison = Business-As-Usual. TPD = 2-day summer workshop (Res/Dev trainer) plus daily lesson plans. Subject = math (STEM); grades 6-8 (mostly 7-8); Low SES (~74% subsidized lunch). 18-week intervention.
problems: SAMPLE IS STUDENTS WITH DISABILITIES (special-education resource rooms; MMD/OHI/SLD/autism/EBD) - flag for meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Effect sizes are the AUTHORS' OWN reported Hedges' g (Table 3 'ES' column, p.432): g = gamma010 / s_pool, where gamma010 is the HLM pretest+covariate-adjusted EAI-vs-BAU impact coefficient and s_pool is the pooled UNADJUSTED student-level posttest SD (Table 3 footnote). The authors did not report SEs for ES nor an explicit small-sample J factor (J~0.998 here, negligible); g_se/g_var were derived centrally as g_se = impact_se / s_pool with s_pool back-computed from |gamma010|/ES so the SE is on the same standardized scale (g_var = g_se^2). The HLM is a 3-level model (students in teachers in schools), so impact estimate + SE are cluster-adjusted (cluster_adjusted=true). ICCs were 'not reported but available from the first author' - NEVER guessed, left null; n_clusters = 31 schools recorded. Independent recompute of s_pool from Table 2 posttest SDs reproduces the reported ES for 3 of 4 overall measures (PS1-PS2 .40 vs reported .39; ITBS Computation .45 vs .44; ITBS PS&DI -.04 vs reported magnitude .04); for the Fractions Computation Test my pooled-SD recompute gives ~1.18 vs reported 1.00 because the EAI posttest SD (13.70) far exceeds BAU (6.65) - authors likely used an alternate/capped pooling; authors' headline ES=1.00 retained. ITBS PS&DI: authors report ES magnitude .04 but gamma010 = -0.15 (favors BAU, non-significant); g recorded NEGATIVE to honour 'positive = favors TPD'. n_t=159 / n_c=176 are full-sample group sizes; HLM per-measure valid-posttest n (FCT 319, PS 324, ITBS-C 317, ITBS-PS 327) are in each record's notes. The 20 reported subscale ES values (10 Fractions-Computation, 4 PS, 6 ITBS-Computation) are components of these four composites and are summarized in notes rather than added as separate rows.

effect_sizes.arm_label: EAI (Enhanced Anchored Instruction blended curriculum) vs BAU
effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' reported Hedges' g (Table 3 ES). g = gamma010 / s_pool; gamma010 = HLM pretest+covariate-adjusted impact, s_pool = pooled unadjusted student-level posttest SD (Table 3 footnote). g_se = impact_se / s_pool (s_pool back-derived from gamma010/ES). My own pooled-SD recompute gives ~1.18 (unequal posttest SDs 13.70 vs 6.65); authors' headline 1.00 retained.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.432 Table 3 (total row); means/SDs p.432 Table 2
effect_sizes.notes: Headline researcher-developed fraction-computation outcome (RQ1), p<.001, n=319 valid posttest in HLM. Subsumes 10 subscales (Addition Overall/Simple/Mixed, Subtraction Overall/Simple/Mixed, Like/Unlike Denominator, No-rewrite/Rewrite), ES range .73-1.00, all p<.001.

effect_sizes.arm_label: EAI (Enhanced Anchored Instruction blended curriculum) vs BAU
effect_sizes.g_method: Authors' reported Hedges' g (Table 3 ES). g = gamma010 / s_pool (HLM pretest+covariate-adjusted impact / pooled unadjusted posttest SD). g_se = impact_se / s_pool (s_pool back-derived from gamma010/ES). Independent pooled-SD recompute reproduces ES (.40 vs reported .39).

effect_sizes.notes: Headline researcher-developed problem-solving outcome (RQ2), p<.05, n=324 valid posttest in HLM. Subsumes 4 subscales: Ratios & Proportional Relationships (ES .61, p<.01), Measurement & Data (.16 ns), Number & Operations-Fractions (.15 ns), Geometry/Graphing (.57, p<.01).
